newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIANTS' SNOW HAS FRACTURED EYE SOCKET.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIANTS' SNOW HAS FRACTURED EYE SOCKET.

text.p: J.T. Snow of the San Francisco Giants suffered fractured left eye socket when he was hit by a Randy Johnson pitch during a Cactus League game on Tuesday.

The Giants announced Wednesday that a CT scan revealed a fracture of Snow's lower left eye orbit. The 29-year-old first baseman will be under observation for the next 7-to-10 days before a determination can be made about how long he will be sidelined.
Dr. Randall Tozer, who examined Snow, said Snow's vision was blurred due to the enormous amount of swelling around the eye, but added the health of the eye was good.
Johnson, the Seattle Mariners ace, had retired the first five batters he faced before throwing a pitch high and inside to Snow, who attempted to get out of the way.
The ball deflected off Snow's wrist and up into his face. X-rays on his wrist were negative, but Snow also suffered a laceration of his left eyelid.

Johnson, who is attempting a comeback after undergoing back surgery, rushed to Snow and knelt beside him after the errant pitch. Snow was removed from the field on a stretcher and taken to the hospital.
Snow is in his first season with the Giants after being acquired in a trade with the Anaheim Angels for pitchers Allen Watson and Fausto Macey.
